subject: dlply of print yields duplicate results

messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: dlply of print yields duplicate results
parts:
Hi All,

I've been dlplying various functions, getting one result per .variable level as expected. Then I applied the print function and got the printout twice, unlabeled by group then labeled. Any idea why?

The program below demonstrates the situation.

Thanks,
Bob

group     <- rep(c("A", "B"), each  = 4)
treatment <- rep(c("A", "B"), times = 4)
score     <- 1:8
mydata    <- data.frame(group, treatment, score)
mydata

dlply(mydata, .(group), print)  # Prints twice
dlply(mydata, .(group), numcolwise(mean))  # Works fine
dlply(mydata, .(group), summary)  # Works fine

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: dlply of print yields duplicate results
parts:
Hi Bob,

The results are printed twice because print() invisibly returns it's
argument (see ?print). So you are printing twice -- once explicitly in
the print call, and then implicitly printing the return value of the
dlply call. You will see the same behavior with

by(mydata, mydata$group, print)

Another way to see what's going on is to assign the results:

x <- dlply(mydata, .(group), print) # prints only once

so your original example is equivalent to

x <- dlply(mydata, .(group), print); x

Best,
Ista
